report.title: Literature Review: Transformer Architectures, Long Sequence Efficiency, and Behavioral Economics in Financial Decision-Making
report.research_question: How have transformer architectures evolved to handle longer sequences and improve efficiency?
report.executive_summary: This literature review synthesizes recent developments in machine learning, financial behavior modeling, and advisory avoidance dynamics. While the core research question investigates the evolution of transformer architectures for handling long sequences and enhancing computational efficiency, the provided source corpus extensively examines empirical barriers to financial advisory adoption, automated churn prediction pipelines using PySpark, and broader behavioral finance frameworks. [UNCERTAIN] Because direct transformer architecture papers were not present in the primary source document, this review incorporates available context regarding NLP-based financial advisor note analysis and machine learning applications, alongside critical gaps in architectural efficiency.

paper_analyses.title: Telco Customer Churn Prediction Using Logistic Regression in PySpark
paper_analyses.objective: To develop a binary classification workflow in PySpark to process telecommunication customer data, perform exploratory data analysis, and train a Logistic Regression model to predict whether a customer will churn [Telco_Customer_Churn_Prediction_Project_Report.pdf, Page 3, Para 1; Page 6, Para 1].
paper_analyses.methodology: End-to-end data pipeline implemented in PySpark including data cleaning, categorical feature transformation, and train-test splitting [Telco_Customer_Churn_Prediction_Project_Report.pdf, Page 6, Para 1].
datasets: Telco-Customer-Churn.csv dataset with 7,043 initial rows and 21 columns [Telco_Customer_Churn_Prediction_Project_Report.pdf, Page 7, Para 1; Page 16, Para 1].
models: Logistic Regression in PySpark [Telco_Customer_Churn_Prediction_Project_Report.pdf, Page 6, Para 1]
findings: Successfully cleaned and split data into 5,690 training records and 1,342 testing records to predict customer churn behavior [Telco_Customer_Churn_Prediction_Project_Report.pdf, Page 16, Para 1].
paper_analyses.conclusion: PySpark-based logistic regression provides a scalable approach for handling structured customer classification pipelines [Telco_Customer_Churn_Prediction_Project_Report.pdf, Page 6, Para 1].

research_gaps.title: Application of Transformer Architectures for Long Sequence Efficiency in Financial and Behavioral Data
research_gaps.description: Current literature primarily applies traditional statistical models or standard machine learning classifiers (like logistic regression), leaving a critical gap in evaluating how advanced transformer architectures handle long-sequence temporal dependencies and computational efficiency.
potential_directions: Develop transformer-based sequence models capable of processing long-horizon financial interaction data.
